subject: Physical segmentation & IO mapping for Private Cluster
messages:
From: Luke Meyers <luke.meyers@terrahealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — physical segmentation + IO questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As we start mapping our racks for the pilot site I wanted to surface a couple of constraints so we can lock down a recommended node layout:

- We have two isolated datacenter rooms in Building B (A and B racks). No east-west L2 stretch between them; routing only at the top-of-rack spine.
- The ops team prefers local NVMe for model serving cache, but wants the ability to tier to a SAN for long-term artifacts.
- Our security team requires control-plane isolation: control plane components must not share subnets with worker host management interfaces.

Can Redwood provide a short prescription: recommended node roles, NIC partitioning (mgmt vs data vs storage), and a suggested PV strategy for ephemeral cache vs persistent artifacts? Attached is our site inventory.

Appreciate any high-level pointer before we schedule the on-site workshop next week.

Luke
Luke Meyers
Infrastructure Lead, TerraHealth
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Luke Meyers <luke.meyers@terrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — physical segmentation + IO questions

Hi Luke — thanks for the inventory and the clear constraints. Quick written summary below; we can expand during the workshop.

Top-level recommendation (short):
- 3-tier node roles per rack: control plane (3x), inference workers (N, depending on throughput), and storage gateway (1–2 per site).
- NIC split: 1x mgmt (1GbE) out-of-band, 2x data (25/40GbE) for pod traffic (bonded), 1x storage (10/25GbE) dedicated to SAN/NAS if used.
- PV strategy: ephemeral local NVMe for token/KV cache (CSI-local with eviction policy), replicated block store on SAN for model artifacts (ReadWriteMany for model pulls), plus a small NFS/SMB for logs/diagnostics.

Key security / network notes:
- Control plane on dedicated subnet with strict ACLs; BGP on spine to enforce routing policies between rooms.
- Use VLANs + SVI on the spine switches; avoid L2 stretch across rooms to reduce blast radius.

I'll attach a short diagram and a draft node-role mapping. Next steps: I can put together a one-page MAD (minimal acceptable design) and a runbook checklist for the on-site day. Can Marissa and Karthik weigh in on the PV fallback pattern and kernel-level tuning?

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding some specifics from the operations perspective:

- Node counts: suggest starting with 3 control-plane (dedicated), 6 inference worker nodes (2 racks, 3 each) for the pilot to allow rack-failure tolerance, and 2 storage gateway nodes clustered for model pulls.
- NVMe sizing: cache partitions should default to 300–400GB per worker for model KV cache; set fsync policies for eviction-friendly workloads.
- Storage fallback: model artifacts staged to a thin-provisioned SAN (iSCSI) with a background sync/garbage collection job to avoid burst downloads during restarts.

Attachment: small checklist for on-site validation (power redundancy, NIC mapping, switch port inventory). I'll add this to the Drive link.

Marissa

Luke — short answers inline, and confirmed for Oct 20th.

> 1) NVMe headroom for growth
Plan for 1.5x operational headroom (so if current active model set uses ~300GB, provision 450GB per worker); we recommend monitoring with the built-in KV cache metrics and keeping 20% free as eviction safety. We'll provide a small automation that flags growth >70% sustained for 24h.

> 2) ACL templates
We'll share a starter ACL: allow management VLAN CIDR -> control-plane API ports (6443, 2379-2380 for etcd), allow ops jump-box IPs, block worker CIDRs from reaching the control-plane mgmt interface. Use host-based firewall on control-plane nodes to enforce the final layer.

Action items before workshop (assigned):
- Avery: MAD one-pager + diagram (attached: network-segmentation-proposal_v1.drawio)
- Karthik: PV fallback recipe + kernel tuning notes (will attach nvme-lifecycle-recommendations.pdf)
- Marissa: on-site validation checklist and port mapping template (see terrahealth_site_inventory.xlsx)
